name: Casa Muffoletto
overview: A narrow, tall corner town house in Gratteri, in the Madonie mountains above Cefalù — four storeys plus attic. The main façade faces Largo Pietra Rossa (front door at no. 2), with the angled side wall along via Pietra Rossa. The lower three floors are essentially one main room each, stacked around a dog-leg staircase; the third floor widens out with several smaller rooms and two terraces. This site is the living record of every room — what's there now, what we want it to become, and the works to get there.

style.direction: Draft — to agree together. Working hypothesis: a Sicilian mountain-village house, done with restraint. Warm lime-plastered walls, local stone and terracotta, chestnut and oak, linen — with Sicilian maiolica (Santo Stefano di Camastra is just along the coast) used as the decorative accent rather than everywhere. Respect what is original to the house.
principles: Keep and restore original features before replacing them (stone door surround, iron balconies, old floors)
One calm base palette through the whole house, with colour concentrated per room
Breathable, mineral finishes — lime and silicate paints on old masonry
Sicilian maiolica as a deliberate accent: a bathroom floor, a splashback, a stair riser — not everywhere
Layered lighting in every room: ambient, task and accent
Small rooms work hard: built-ins, niches and every centimetre planned
